newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Alusuisse plans Singapore chemical plant.
newsitem.headline: Alusuisse plans Singapore chemical plant.

text.p: Alusuisse-Lonza Holding AG said its chemicals division would build a Singapore plant to produce purified isophtalic acid (PIA), a plastic imtermediate used in making certain kinds of resins, coatings and paints.
Total capital investment would be $125 million, Alusuisse said. The plant would produce 70,000 tonnes a year when it came on line at the end of 1998.

The plant will be a joint venture held 80 percent by the Swiss group, which also makes packaging and aluminium products, and 20 percent by the governmental agency Economic Development Board of Singapore, Alusuisse said in a statement.
Alusuisse said the plant would be built on the island of Palau Sakra, west of Singapore's central business district, with a total of 75,000 square metres, including land reserves for future projects.
Alusuisse said the manufacturing process would be based on a proprietary liquid phase oxidation technology developed by its chemical division, Lonza.

"The realisation of the isophthalic acid plant will enable Lonza to broaden its product range, to participate in the fast growing Asian-Pacific market and to strengthen its position as a leading manifacturer of plastic intermediates," it said.

Alusuisse said PIA was a plastic intermediate used in manufacturing unsaturated polyester resins and environmentally-friendly, water-based, solvent-free coatings and paints as well as PET bottle-grade resins.
